channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest
channel.description: This week's upcoming Gov-Hub meetings and community events across the Telluride region (Town of Telluride, Mountain Village, San Miguel County, the Sheridan Opera House, The Alibi, Wilkinson Library, KOTO, telluride.com, and more).

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Nov 11–17
item.description: The most consequential meeting this week is San Miguel County's Planning Commission on November 12, where proposed amendments to the Affordable Housing Impact Mitigation Fee — LUC Section 5-1303 — are on the table alongside broader housing incentive ideas; that fee structure directly shapes whether workforce housing gets built here, so it's worth paying attention. SMART's board also meets virtually that same day to act on three resolutions, including an amendment to the Executive Director's employment agreement and a resolution on federal transit grant program changes, with a gondola project update in the mix. On the lighter side, the KOTO Ski Swap kicks off Friday and there's ski film action at the Sheridan Opera House on Saturday.

item.title: [Wed, Nov 11] How Money Became God: Online Author Talk with Paul Vigna
item.description: 🎫 Wilkinson Public Library 📍 Wilkinson Public Library 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM · Join us for an eye-opening conversation with veteran journalist Paul Vigna as we examine his provocative book, The Almightier: How Money Became God, Greed Became Virtue, and Debt Became Sin , in which he explores the question: how did money go from a tool of commerce into the dominant faith of modern society? In The Almightier , Vigna takes readers on a sweeping historical journey from Renaissance Florence to today's global financial markets, revealing how wealth accumulation evolved from a moral failing into an unspoken civic virtue. He uncovers the forgotten history of money, tracing the uneasy and often accidental alliance between wealth and religion as it developed from ancient city-states to today's secular world, where religious devotion has receded and greed has stepped in to fill the void. …

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Planning Commission Meeting — 2026-11-12
item.description:
San Miguel County • 2026-11-12
Two substantive items on the November 12 agenda. The morning work session takes up proposed amendments to LUC Section 5-1303 — the Affordable Housing Impact Mitigation Fee — along with a broader discussion of housing incentive ideas. That fee structure has real implications for how (and whether) workforce housing gets built across the county, so the conversation is worth watching. After lunch, the commission moves to a formal land use application: a county-initiated rezoning of a portion of Placerville Park around the fire station, from Forestry, Agriculture, and Open (F) to Public (P) — a housekeeping move to bring the zoning in line with the site's actual public use.
⚡ Why it matters: Proposed fee changes to county affordable housing mitigation could reshape workforce housing.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Vending Subcommittee - Nov 12 2026 — 2026-11-12
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-11-12
The Vending Subcommittee meets to approve minutes from September 23 and to act on the remaining open permit for the 2026-2027 winter vending season at Gondola Plaza. The Gondola Plaza East spot was already awarded to Mini Deli (PhilAm, LLC) in September. Up now is Gondola Plaza West, where The Gyro Cart — a returning vendor with eight consecutive summer seasons on Oak Street East — has submitted a late application to operate through the winter season serving lamb gyros, chicken shawarma, Greek salads, and related items, 11am to 4pm. Staff recommends granting the permit. Winter vending permits run $250 for the season.
⚡ Why it matters: Final winter vending permit for Gondola Plaza West decided — The Gyro Cart on the line.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation - Nov 12 2026 — 2026-11-12
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-11-12
SMART's board convenes virtually to act on three resolutions: routine agenda/minutes approval, a resolution of support for comments on proposed changes to a federal Capital Investments Grant Program, and an amendment to the Executive Director's employment agreement. The gondola project gets a verbal update — always worth watching given the ongoing SMART Ballot Issue 3A context. The board also receives the November operations report and Q3 2026 performance data before closing with an executive session on personnel matters concerning the Executive Director position.
⚡ Why it matters: Board votes on federal transit grant comments and Executive Director contract amendment.

item.title: [Fri, Nov 13] The Creative Exchange at Telluride Arts HQ
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Telluride Arts HQ, TELLURIDE The Creative Exchange is a brand-new monthly series by Telluride Arts designed for the artists and creatives who call Telluride home. It’s a space where emerging and established artists gather to share the knowledge, skills, and stories that fuel their work. Think of it as an open source model for creativity—where we learn from each other, swap ideas, and help strengthen one another’s practice. Each session is hosted by local artists and creative leaders who bring their own perspectives, techniques, and creative journeys into the room. Topics may span everything from the business of art and professional development, to creative process, storytelling, collaboration, and the philosophical underpinnings of making art. Whether you’re a full-time working artist, an educator, a student, a maker, or simply someone curious about creative expression, the Creative Exchange is open to you. …

item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Montrose County Event Center Discover agricultural innovation, explore practical ideas, and connect with your Western Slope neighbors at the free 2026 Western Colorado Farm & Ranch Innovation Expo, November 13–14 at the Montrose County Event Center. Hosted by the Western Colorado Soil Health Committee, this welcoming gathering brings together farmers, ranchers, gardeners, water leaders, educators, students, businesses, and community members for demonstrations, exhibits, presentations, and conversations. FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 13 Expo hours: noon–7 p.m. Explore agricultural equipment, technology, and exhibits, with water-related demonstrations beginning at 2 p.m. following the West Slope Water Summit. Meet vendors and producers, ask questions, and discover practical irrigation and water-management approaches. Also on Friday: West Slope Water Summit, 7:30 a.m.–2 p.m. This free gathering explores Western Colorado’s water outlook, watershed health, and agriculture’s connection to water, and includes an FFA student research presentation. Separate advance registration is required, with complimentary breakfast and lunch for registered participants. …
